 Marquez explains shock late crash that kept MotoGP title fight open
 Eden Hannigan
 21 Nov 2026 
 — 2 min read 
 Marc Marquez admitted that underestimating the wet conditions led to his crash out of the Portimao sprint race whilst on the brink of the 2026 MotoGP title.
 Marquez was running third, and on course for an eighth premier-class championship with nearest rival Jorge Martin languishing in seventh, but crashed at Turn 8 on the penultimate lap of the race to delay his coronation.
 Race organisers had been forced to bring the sprint forwards by 30 minutes due the inclement weather expected on Saturday afternoon. 
 The rain arrived early enough to bring the white flag out on just the second lap of the sprint, with the conditions becoming increasingly difficult towards the end of the 12-lap dash.
 It is these wet conditions, Marquez admitted, that led to his crash as he underestimated just how much water had collected at Turn 8 with two laps to go. 
 "It was a very difficult sprint race, especially in that lap when it started to rain more," Marquez told TNT Sports. "When I arrived in that corner, I didn’t realise it was so wet in that corner. 
 "In the beginning, it was already very tricky. It was raining - especially on this kind of track, you don’t realise a lot but the asphalt is quite wet."
 Asked in his main media session afterwards if he had maybe "relaxed" too much given he was outscoring main rival Jorge Martin and had brother Alex protecting him from behind, Marquez insisted he had been anything but relaxed as the conditions changed.
 "Yeah, the conditions [for sealing the title] were perfect, but no, I was not relaxed," Marquez replied.
 "I was relaxed the last five laps, I was flowing well, the lap time was good, but when I saw the spray, the rain flags, then I was not relaxed and even at the previous corner I was extra careful because it was downhill.
 "In the acceleration of [Turn] 6, I feel like 'OK, the asphalt is OK', because normally you test the asphalt on gas, it's less risky, but then on that Turn 8 I was too optimistic."
 Marquez also explained that part of the reason he was caught out by the conditions was being one of the first riders to encounter the increased rain at the corner, despite previously having confidence with his Ducati set-up.
 He was leading a pack of bikes that had fallen away from top two Marco Bezzecchi and Raul Fernandez.
 "When it was dry, it was good," Marquez said. "But, unlucky for us, the last two laps again started that spray and I arrived in that Turn 8, I was not conscious maybe that it was so wet.
 "The first one of the group that arrives usually makes the mistake and this time I did the mistake. 
 "It is like it is, one and a half laps to achieve our goal, but tomorrow we will have another opportunity."
 Marquez remains firmly on course to clinch the title by the end of the Portimao weekend, as he still leads Martin by 55 points and Bezzecchi by 62, and only 37 will be available at the Valencia finale.
 He said he wouldn't be paying any attention to the maths permutations in Sunday's grand prix and would just take a "doesn't matter, finish the race" approach.
